newsitem.title: SPAIN: Colombia to meet 18 pct inflation target - Ocampo.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to meet 18 pct inflation target - Ocampo.

text.p: Colombia is on course to meet its 18 percent inflation target for 1997 but the central government deficit may edge over its forecast 3.2 percent, finance minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said on Monday.
"We are now at 19.5 percent. I think we are well on target to achieve 18 percent (inflation) this year," he said in an interview at the Inter-American Development Bank annual meeting.
He said approval of a 16.9 percent wage rise for government workers and teachers was a positive achievement.
"I think that was certainly a good achievement for the government especially since inflation last year was 21.6 percent," he said.
But he added that the central government deficit could come in a little over Colombia's original 3.2 percent target, at between 3.2 and 3.4 percent.
"The central government budget deficit will be reduced by half a percent of GDP -- it will be between 3.2 and 3.4 percent," he said.

"Even if you include the higher wage bill, the total central government budget will only increase by 12 percent in nominal terms, and decline by 7.0 percent in real terms," he added. (( --IADB newsroom +34 3 424 2659 ))
